description: The one registry of performance metrics, metric types, training objectives and evaluation profiles that every catalog model's `metrics` record names by id. For a quantity the Model Cycle engine computes, `definition` and `formula` are the engine's own text (packages/ml-engine/src/cycle/report.py DEFINITIONS, pinned by packages/ml-engine/tests/test_metric_registry.py) and `engine_id` is the engine's column name.

availabilityValues.computed: The Model Cycle computes it and lands it in the run record.
availabilityValues.computed_not_recorded: The adapter computes it during training but it reaches only the terminal log or an unnamed column.
availabilityValues.derivable: It can be computed from the eight run-record tables without a rerun, and no code does so yet.
availabilityValues.not_computed: Nothing in the dashboard computes it today.

roleValues.primary: The number that says whether the model did its job.
roleValues.secondary: Supports or qualifies the primary number.

faithfulToSpecificationValues.faithful: The runnable adapter is the algorithm the specification describes.
faithfulToSpecificationValues.partial: The runnable adapter implements the core mechanism and leaves named parts out.
faithfulToSpecificationValues.stand_in: The runnable adapter is a different estimator standing in for the specification.
faithfulToSpecificationValues.no_specification: The runnable model has no catalog specification.

probabilitySourceValues.own_likelihood_probability: The probability of up is the model's own likelihood output: the sigmoid or softmax of what it was trained to make probable.
probabilitySourceValues.frequency_or_vote_share: The probability of up is a share: the fraction of trees, neighbours or leaf samples that say up.
probabilitySourceValues.validation_fitted_curve: A score or a forecast is turned into a probability by a logistic curve fitted on the fold's validation bars.
probabilitySourceValues.validation_temperature_only: The model's own probability is rescaled by one temperature fitted on the fold's validation bars.
probabilitySourceValues.model_implied_tail_probability: The probability that the horizon move is above zero under the model's own predictive distribution.
probabilitySourceValues.policy_action_share: The share of the policy's action probability, or of its sampled actions, that is long.
probabilitySourceValues.classifier_trained_on_generated_rows: A classifier trained only on rows the generator produced, read on real bars.
probabilitySourceValues.learned_head_on_code: A small classifier head trained on the model's latent code, state or embedding.
probabilitySourceValues.mean_of_base_learners: The average of several base learners' probabilities.

priceForecastSourceValues.own_model: The price forecast is the model itself; the direction call is derived from it.
priceForecastSourceValues.own_model_shared_encoder: A price head on the same network that makes the direction call.
priceForecastSourceValues.second_model_same_family: A second model of the same family, fitted separately on the move in points.
priceForecastSourceValues.readout: A simple readout (a cell mean, a state's mean move, a slope times the score), not a fitted forecaster.
priceForecastSourceValues.none: The model makes no price forecast.

checkpointSelectedByValues.validation_logarithmic_loss: The step with the lowest logarithmic loss on the fold's validation bars is kept.
checkpointSelectedByValues.validation_huber_loss: The step with the lowest Huber loss on the fold's validation bars is kept.
checkpointSelectedByValues.validation_tape_utility: The step with the highest simulated trading utility on the fold's validation bars is kept.
checkpointSelectedByValues.none: No checkpoint selection: the final fit is used.

metricTypes.name: Proper scoring rule
metricTypes.questionItAnswers: Are the stated odds or the stated forecast distribution honest? The score is best only when the model states the true probabilities. Held-out log-likelihood belongs here.

metricTypes.name: Calibration and sharpness
metricTypes.questionItAnswers: When the model says 60 percent (or an 80 percent interval), does it happen that often, and does the model ever commit away from its average?

metricTypes.name: Discrimination and ranking
metricTypes.questionItAnswers: Does the output order the outcomes, independent of whether its scale is right? Only threshold-free quantities belong here.

metricTypes.name: Classification at the 0.5 cut
metricTypes.questionItAnswers: How good are the hard up or down calls made by cutting the probability of up at 0.5? These depend on the scale and prior of the probability.

metricTypes.name: Point-forecast error
metricTypes.questionItAnswers: How far is a single-number forecast from what happened, in the units of the thing forecast?

metricTypes.name: Distributional assumption check
metricTypes.questionItAnswers: Do the model's own assumptions (variance family, independent residuals, independent components) hold on unseen rows?

metricTypes.name: Reconstruction and representation quality
metricTypes.questionItAnswers: How much is lost by the compression, and does the learned code keep what matters?

metricTypes.name: Structure validity
metricTypes.questionItAnswers: Are the groups, states or graph the model found tight, apart and real?

metricTypes.name: Sample fidelity, diversity and novelty
metricTypes.questionItAnswers: Do generated or simulated samples look like real ones, cover every kind of real one, and avoid copying training rows?

metricTypes.name: Decision return
metricTypes.questionItAnswers: What did the decisions earn, net of costs, in the units of the reward?

metricTypes.name: Risk-adjusted return
metricTypes.questionItAnswers: What was earned per unit of a stated risk measure (spread, downside, drawdown, losses)?

metricTypes.name: Risk and cost
metricTypes.questionItAnswers: What path, drawdown, exposure, turnover and cost came with that return?

metricTypes.name: Solution quality and constraint satisfaction
metricTypes.questionItAnswers: How close to the best answer of the stated problem is the returned answer, and does it obey the stated constraints or rules?

metricTypes.name: Convergence and efficiency
metricTypes.questionItAnswers: Did the fit, search, sampler or solver finish its job, and at what cost in steps? Never a score of the model.

metricTypes.name: Stability, selection optimism and sampling uncertainty
metricTypes.questionItAnswers: Does the result survive a new seed, the next fold, a perturbed input, switching off the model's special part, or the luck of the sample and of the search that picked it?

metricTypes.name: Interpretability and behaviour
metricTypes.questionItAnswers: What is the model doing inside (which rule, expert, state, action), described but never scored?

metricTypes.name: Coverage and baseline
metricTypes.questionItAnswers: How many bars or rules were scored, and what does the same series give with no model at all?

metrics.definition: How surprised the model was by what happened, averaged; punishes confident wrong calls hard. 0.693 is a coin flip.
metrics.baseline: logarithmic loss of always quoting the fold's training up share; ln 2 only for class-weighted models
metrics.reading: Over scored bars (label resolved, horizon crosses no session gap, absolute move above label_threshold_ticks times tick size, model predicted) it is minus the mean of y times ln(p) plus (1 minus y) times ln(1 minus p); y is 1 when the close label_horizon_bars ahead is above this bar's close; p is clipped only at machine epsilon, so one confident miss at exactly 0 or 1 costs about 36 nats. Not annualised.

metrics.fullName: Logarithmic loss skill versus the training base rate
metrics.definition: One minus the logarithmic loss divided by the logarithmic loss of quoting the fold's training up share on every scored bar.
metrics.engineSource: needs training_up_fraction; store.py:113-132 holds only majority_class_up

metrics.definition: The log loss of the scored up bars and the log loss of the scored down bars, averaged with each class carrying half whatever its share of the bars; the proper score that matches a model fitted with class-balanced weights. P(up) is clipped at machine epsilon as in the log loss. 0.693 is always saying 0.5.
metrics.formula: 0.5 x mean over up bars of -ln(p) + 0.5 x mean over down bars of -ln(1 - p)
metrics.reading: Mean of the logarithmic loss over scored up bars and the logarithmic loss over scored down bars, each class carrying half; the proper score that matches a class-weighted fit.

metrics.definition: The mean squared gap between P(up) and the outcome (1 up, 0 down); 0.25 is always saying 0.5.
metrics.baseline: brier score of the training up share
metrics.reading: Mean over scored bars of the squared difference between the probability of up and the 1-or-0 outcome; bounded, so it can grade outputs that reach exactly 0 or 1.

metrics.definition: How much better the Brier score is than always forecasting the base rate; above 0 beats the base rate.
metrics.formula: 1 - Brier score / (base rate x (1 - base rate))
metrics.reading: One minus the Brier score divided by base times one minus base, where base is the scored test bars' own up share, known only in hindsight; a training-up-share variant is an engine gap.

metrics.definition: The part of the Brier score that is miscalibration (Murphy 1973, ten equal-width bins).
metrics.formula: sum over bins of n_k (mean p_k - observed_k)^2 / N
metrics.reading: Over 10 equal-width probability bins, the bin-size-weighted mean squared gap between mean predicted probability and observed up share; with binned forecasts reliability minus resolution plus uncertainty does not sum exactly to the Brier score.

metrics.definition: The part of the Brier score that is separation: how far each bin's outcome rate sits from the base rate (Murphy 1973).
metrics.formula: sum over bins of n_k (observed_k - base rate)^2 / N
metrics.reading: Over the same 10 equal-width bins, the bin-size-weighted mean squared gap between each bin's observed up share and the scored bars' up share.

metrics.definition: The average gap between the probability forecast and how often up happened, over ten equal-width probability bins weighted by their bar counts.
metrics.formula: sum over bins of (bars in bin / scored bars) x |observed up share - mean p|
metrics.reading: Bin-share-weighted mean absolute gap between observed up share and mean predicted probability over 10 equal-width bins on scored bars; shown with the occupied-bin count because probabilities near 0.5 fill two bins.

metrics.definition: The largest such gap in any non-empty bin.
metrics.formula: max over bins of |observed up share - mean p|
metrics.reading: Largest absolute gap between observed up share and mean predicted probability over the non-empty equal-width bins.

metrics.definition: The slope of a logistic regression of the outcome (1 up, 0 down) on the log-odds of P(up) over scored bars, with P(up) clipped to [0.000001, 0.999999]. It uses no bins. 1 means the probabilities are on the right scale; below 1 they are too extreme (over-confident), above 1 too timid.
metrics.formula: fit y ~ sigmoid(a + b x ln(p / (1 - p))) by maximum likelihood; report b
metrics.reading: Slope of a logistic regression of the outcome on the log-odds of the probability of up over scored bars; bin-free; 1 means the scale is right, below 1 over-confident.

metrics.definition: The intercept of the same regression with the slope held at 1, in log-odds. 0 means no overall lean; above 0 up happened more often than the probabilities said, below 0 less often.
metrics.formula: fit y ~ sigmoid(a + ln(p / (1 - p))) by maximum likelihood; report a
metrics.reading: Intercept of the same regression with the slope fixed at 1; 0 means no overall lean toward up or down.

metrics.fullName: Sharpness of the probability of up
metrics.definition: How far the model's probabilities spread: the standard deviation of P(up). Sharp is only good when it is also calibrated.
metrics.reading: Sample standard deviation (ddof 1) of the probability of up over scored bars; a property of the forecasts alone.

metrics.fullName: Scored bars with probability of up exactly 0 or 1
metrics.definition: Scored bars where the model gave a probability of up of exactly 0 or exactly 1; each one that misses costs about 36 in the log loss.
metrics.formula: count of scored bars with p <= 0 or p >= 1
metrics.reading: Count of scored bars whose probability of up equals 0 or 1; each such miss costs about 36 nats of logarithmic loss.

metrics.definition: How many different values the probability of up took on the scored bars; with only a handful, ROC AUC and average precision are curves of a few points.
metrics.reading: Number of distinct values the probability of up took on a fold's scored bars; ranking metrics on a few levels are a curve of a few points.

metrics.fullName: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve
metrics.definition: The chance that a randomly chosen up bar got a higher P(up) than a randomly chosen down bar; 0.5 is no ranking skill.
metrics.formula: area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of P(up)
metrics.reading: Probability that a random scored up bar got a higher probability of up than a random scored down bar, ties counting half; null with one class.

metrics.definition: The area under the precision-recall curve of P(up): ranking skill for the up class, read against the up base rate.
metrics.formula: sum over thresholds of (recall step x precision)
metrics.reading: Area under the precision-recall curve of the probability of up against the actual up label on scored bars.

metrics.definition: The share of scored bars whose direction the model called correctly.
metrics.reading: Share of scored bars where the call (up when probability of up is at least 0.5) equals the actual direction.

metrics.definition: How much the model's accuracy beats the majority-class baseline, in accuracy points.
metrics.reading: Accuracy minus the accuracy of calling every scored bar the fold's training majority class.

metrics.definition: Accuracy with up and down weighted equally, so a lopsided market cannot flatter it.
metrics.reading: Mean of the per-class recall over the classes present in the actual labels of scored bars.

metrics.definition: The correlation between the calls and the outcomes, from -1 (always wrong) through 0 (no better than chance) to 1; fair under imbalance.
metrics.formula: (TP x TN - FP x FN) / sqrt((TP + FP)(TP + FN)(TN + FP)(TN + FN))
metrics.reading: Correlation between called and actual direction over the four confusion cells of scored bars.

metrics.definition: The harmonic mean of precision and recall for the up class.
metrics.reading: Harmonic mean of precision and recall of the up call on scored bars; precision, recall, their down versions and the macro mean are separate engine ids in the registry.

metrics.definition: The accuracy of calling every scored bar the class most common in its fold's training labels.
metrics.formula: scored bars matching the fold's training majority / scored bars
metrics.reading: Share of scored bars equal to the fold's training majority class (up when the training up share is at least 0.5).

metrics.definition: The share of processed bars that were scored.
metrics.reading: Bars with a known outcome and a prediction divided by processed test bars.

metrics.fullName: Actual up share of scored bars
metrics.definition: The share of scored bars whose price rose over the horizon: the base rate a classifier has to beat.
metrics.formula: scored bars that went up / scored bars
metrics.reading: Scored bars that went up divided by scored bars; a hindsight base rate.

metrics.definition: The share of scored bars the model called up.
metrics.formula: scored bars called up / scored bars
metrics.reading: Scored bars called up divided by scored bars; shown beside every trading metric.

metrics.fullName: Price forecast absolute-error skill versus the no-change forecast
metrics.definition: How much smaller the forecast's error is than the no-change forecast's; above 0 beats no-change.
metrics.formula: 1 - forecast mean absolute error / no-change mean absolute error
metrics.reading: One minus the mean absolute error of the forecast move divided by the mean absolute actual move on the same resolved bars; the forecast is the model output times the causal trailing move scale, rounded to the tick before scoring; no label threshold; consistent for a median forecast.

metrics.fullName: Price forecast squared-error skill versus the no-change forecast
metrics.definition: How much smaller the forecast's mean squared error is than the no-change forecast's, over resolved forecasts; above 0 beats no-change. It is the out-of-sample R-squared against a zero-move benchmark, the skill measure that matches a forecast of the mean move.
metrics.formula: 1 - mean((predicted move - actual move)^2) / mean(actual move^2)
metrics.reading: One minus the mean squared forecast error divided by the mean squared actual move on resolved bars; the out-of-sample R-squared against a zero-move benchmark, consistent for a mean forecast.

metrics.definition: The average size of the gap between the forecast move and the actual move.
metrics.reading: Mean absolute difference between predicted and actual horizon move over resolved forecasts.

metrics.definition: The same error for the no-change forecast (predicted close = this close): the baseline.
metrics.reading: Mean absolute actual horizon move on the same resolved bars: the error of forecasting no move.

metrics.fullName: Price forecast root mean square error
metrics.definition: The error's root mean square; weighs big misses more than the mean absolute error does.
metrics.reading: Square root of the mean squared difference between predicted and actual horizon move.

metrics.definition: Whether the forecasts lean one way: the average signed error. Positive forecasts too high.
metrics.reading: Mean of predicted minus actual horizon move over resolved forecasts.

metrics.definition: The Pearson correlation between the forecast move and the actual move.
metrics.reading: Pearson correlation between predicted and actual horizon move; driven by large moves; a rank version would be a separate metric.

metrics.definition: The share of resolved forecasts whose move had the right sign, over bars where neither move is zero.
metrics.reading: Share of resolved forecasts whose sign equals the sign of the actual move, over bars where both are non-zero after tick rounding; shown with that denominator.

metrics.fullName: Share of bars where the forecast's sign equals the traded call
metrics.definition: The share of processed bars where the sign of the forecast move is the direction the model called, over bars where the forecast move is not zero and a call was made. Below 1, the step that turns the forecast into P(up) shifted or reversed it.
metrics.reading: Share of bars where the sign of the predicted move equals the traded direction; below 1 the validation-fitted curve shifted or inverted the forecast.

metrics.definition: Profit after every cost, marked to market bar by bar.
metrics.reading: Sum over walked test bars of position times price change times point value times contracts minus fill costs. The position follows the sign of the latest call, filled at the next bar's open; a trade ends when the call flips, a stop or target is hit, or the fold ends (flattened at the last close); a bar with no prediction holds the position. long_only, holding_bars, stop and target ticks and contracts change it. For roots other than MNQ the per-side cost is the MNQ account figure, a stated assumption.

metrics.definition: One contract position bought at each fold's first open and sold at its last close, one round trip per fold, summed.
metrics.formula: sum over folds of (last close - first open) x point value x contracts - one round trip
metrics.reading: Per fold, last close minus first open times point value times contracts minus one round trip, summed over folds.

metrics.fullName: Net profit minus buy and hold
metrics.definition: How much the model made beyond holding the market.
metrics.reading: Net profit minus the buy-and-hold baseline of the same folds.

metrics.fullName: Net profit minus the sign-shuffled baseline
metrics.definition: Net profit minus the mean net profit of the same simulator run on this run's calls permuted inside each fold, which keeps the long share and approximate flip count and charges the same costs.
metrics.engineSource: re-run of simulate.py over the predictions table

metrics.fullName: Sharpe ratio (per bar, USD based, annualised)
metrics.definition: Average per-bar profit over its standard deviation, annualized with the run's measured bars per year.
metrics.formula: mean(r) / std(r, ddof 1) x sqrt(bars per year)
metrics.reading: Mean of per-bar net USD (flat bars zero, costs included) over its sample standard deviation, times the square root of bars per year; bars per year is loaded bars divided by calendar years after removing gaps longer than four days (an engine constant) and is recorded in runs.bars_per_year; no risk-free rate; null with fewer than two bars or zero spread. Zero is an arithmetic marker, not a no-skill reference once costs are charged.

metrics.definition: How uncertain the Sharpe estimate is given the sample size and the skew and fat tails of per-bar profit (Lo 2002; Bailey and Lopez de Prado 2012).
metrics.formula: sqrt((1 - skew x SR + (kurtosis - 1) / 4 x SR^2) / (N - 1)) x sqrt(bars per year), SR per bar, kurtosis not excess
metrics.reading: Sampling error of the per-bar Sharpe ratio from the sample's length, skewness and non-excess kurtosis, annualised; assumes independent bars, which overlapping holds violate.

metrics.definition: The probability that the true Sharpe ratio is above zero given this sample, its skew and its fat tails (Bailey and Lopez de Prado 2012).
metrics.formula: Phi(SR x sqrt(N - 1) / sqrt(1 - skew x SR + (kurtosis - 1) / 4 x SR^2)), SR per bar
metrics.reading: Probability that the true per-bar Sharpe ratio exceeds zero given the sample; an inference statement under the same independence assumption.

metrics.definition: Like Sharpe, but only losing bars count as risk.
metrics.formula: mean(r) / sqrt(mean(min(r, 0)^2)) x sqrt(bars per year)
metrics.reading: Mean per-bar net USD over the root mean square of the negative bars taken over all bars, times the square root of bars per year; null with no negative bar.

metrics.definition: Annualized profit over the worst drawdown.
metrics.formula: mean(r) x bars per year / maximum drawdown
metrics.reading: Mean per-bar net USD times bars per year over maximum drawdown in USD; null with zero drawdown.

metrics.definition: What the winners made per dollar the losers lost; above 1 is profitable.
metrics.formula: sum of winning nets / |sum of losing nets|
metrics.reading: Sum of closed winning trades' net USD over the absolute sum of losing trades' net USD, both after costs; null with no trades or no loser.

metrics.definition: The largest fall of the equity curve (starting at 0) from a peak to a later trough.
metrics.formula: max over bars of (running peak - equity)
metrics.reading: Largest fall of cumulative per-bar net USD from its running peak, marked to market each bar, as a positive number.

metrics.definition: Trades opened and closed in this scope.
metrics.reading: Count of closed trades; because a same-direction call is kept without an exit, it counts call flips, stops, targets and fold ends, not predictions.

metrics.definition: The share of closed trades that made money after costs.
metrics.reading: Closed trades with net USD above zero over closed trades; break-even trades count as non-wins.

metrics.definition: What a trade is expected to make from the win rate and the average win and loss.
metrics.formula: win rate x average win - (1 - win rate) x |average loss|
metrics.reading: Win rate times average win minus one minus win rate times the absolute average loss; a missing side contributes zero and break-even trades carry the average-loss weight, so it differs from the average trade.

metrics.definition: The share of bars a position was held through.
metrics.reading: Share of walked bars on which a position was held before or after the bar's fill; with long_only off the engine never goes flat once in a trade, so it describes the engine's rule.

metrics.definition: Commissions, exchange and NFA fees and slippage on every fill.
metrics.reading: Sum over closed trades of two sides of cost_model.json total_per_side times contracts; for roots other than MNQ the figure is the MNQ account figure, a stated assumption.

metrics.fullName: Break-even cost per contract per side
metrics.definition: The cost per contract per side at which the net profit would be zero: the cushion the edge has against costs.
metrics.formula: cost per contract per side + net profit / (2 x contracts traded)
metrics.reading: The per-side cost at which net profit would be zero: cost per contract per side plus net profit over twice the contracts traded.

metrics.definition: How often the model trades.
metrics.reading: Closed trades divided by distinct session days.

metrics.definition: Count, mean, median, standard deviation (ddof 1), bias-corrected skewness and excess kurtosis, 25th and 75th percentiles, minimum and maximum of trade net, bars held, bar net, session-day net, drawdown depth, probability of up and forecast error, per segment.
metrics.formula: count, mean, median, std, skew, excess kurtosis, P25, P75, min, max

metrics.fullName: Standard error of the model-minus-baseline loss difference
metrics.definition: Standard error of the mean per-bar loss difference between the model and its own baseline with a Newey-West variance at label_horizon_bars minus one lags, because consecutive scored bars share future bars.

The adapter's own objective at each logged step on training and validation rows, labelled with the objective id and unit from the model's record; stored today as train_loss and validation_loss with no name.

metrics.fullName: Kept solution's objective on validation minus on training
metrics.definition: The kept solution's own objective on the validation span minus on the training span; valid only where both are the same quantity.
metrics.formula: f(validation) - f(train) at the kept step
metrics.engineSource: epochs table only where step_quantity.same_quantity is true; otherwise not recorded

metrics.definition: Mean pre-clip global gradient norm over an epoch's batches; neural adapters only.

metrics.fullName: Loss surface sharpness (with condition number and valley width)
metrics.definition: Mean absolute second derivative of the loss at the minimum of a filter-normalised grid around the kept weights; neural adapters only.

Median over inner expanding blocks of the fold's training span of the tuning objective (default per-bar Sharpe ratio from the real simulator); a selection score, optimistic by construction, the same for every model; an undefined block scores 0.0, which for a minimised logarithmic loss is the best possible value.

metrics.fullName: Search score minus the fold's test value
metrics.definition: The best trial's search objective minus the same quantity on the fold's test walk.
Number of candidate solutions, rules or trials scored on training data before one was kept.
metrics.engineSource: trials table for Optuna; a searcher's own population is not recorded

metrics.definition: Mean gate probability per expert over scored bars.
metrics.engineSource: data/models/<id>/gate_routings.json (file, not a lake table); engine.py:1181-1203

metrics.definition: Mean entropy of the gate's probabilities per bar.
Mean entropy of attention weights over the window or over base models; an explanation aid.

metrics.fullName: Architecture behaviour shares (spike rate, memory slot usage, capsule routing agreement, slot assignment, decision leaf usage)
metrics.definition: The usage share of the architecture's own routing unit named in the model record; group entry whose members (spike_rate_fraction, memory_slot_usage_fractions, capsule_routing_agreement, slot_assignment_share, decision_leaf_usage_fractions) are separate registry ids.

metrics.fullName: Share of bars the policy prefers long, short and flat
metrics.definition: Share of bars on which the policy's own preferred action is long, short or flat; the engine overrides flat.
metrics.engineSource: predictions table holds long or short only; the flat share is not recorded

metrics.definition: Mean log density (or a stated lower bound, naming which) the fitted model gives to rows it never trained on; for a hidden Markov model the one-step-ahead predictive log density from the forward filter.
metrics.baseline: single Gaussian fitted to the same training span

metrics.fullName: Held-out log predictive density of the move
metrics.definition: Mean log of the forecast density evaluated at the realised horizon move.
Mean over resolved bars of the integrated squared difference between the forecast cumulative distribution and the step at the realised move; equals mean absolute error for a single-number forecast.

metrics.fullName: Prediction interval coverage by nominal level
metrics.definition: Share of realised moves inside each plotted central forecast interval against its nominal level, with mean interval width; the levels are plotted levels, never pass marks.

Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance between the forecast cumulative distribution evaluated at each realised value (or the realised rank among simulated values) and the uniform distribution, drawn as a histogram.

metrics.fullName: Pinball loss at the fitted quantile level
metrics.definition: Mean of level times (actual minus predicted) when actual is above the prediction and (one minus level) times (predicted minus actual) when below; at level 0.5 it is half the mean absolute error.
metrics.engineSource: predictions table with the registry quantile parameter

metrics.definition: Share of resolved bars whose actual move fell below the predicted quantile, against its level; for a variance forecast the band is built from the forecast variance at stated plotted levels.
Mean over bars of the sum over ordered buckets of the squared difference between cumulative predicted probability and the cumulative observed indicator.

metrics.fullName: Mean deviance of the model's own distribution family
metrics.definition: Twice the mean difference between the log-likelihood of a perfect fit and of the model under the fitted family on held-out rows, reported as deviance explained against the intercept-only fit.
metrics.baseline: intercept-only fit of the same family

metrics.definition: Pearson chi-square over residual degrees of freedom; 1 means the family's variance assumption holds.

metrics.fullName: Quasi-likelihood loss of the variance forecast
metrics.definition: Mean of realised variance over forecast variance minus the log of that ratio minus one, with the proxy stated (squared horizon return).
metrics.baseline: trailing-window variance of the same series

metrics.definition: Ljung-Box p-value on the model's residuals (and on squared standardised residuals for volatility models), with the lag count stated and the degrees of freedom reduced by the fitted parameters.
Among comparable pairs of walks, the share where the one predicted riskier touched its barrier first, with inverse-probability-of-censoring weights, truncated at maximum_hold_bars.

metrics.fullName: Integrated Brier score of the survival curve
metrics.definition: Brier score of 'not yet touched by bar t' with inverse-probability-of-censoring weights, averaged over t up to maximum_hold_bars.
metrics.baseline: unstratified Kaplan-Meier curve of the same training span

metrics.definition: Mean over held-out rows of nearest-other-cluster distance minus own-cluster distance over the larger; computed in the space the method clusters in (the spectral embedding for spectral clustering); valid for compact groups only.
Density sparseness within clusters against density separation between them (Moulavi 2014), reported with the share of rows labelled noise.
Share of rows whose best and second-best map nodes are not grid neighbours; self-organising map only.
Chance-corrected agreement between state labels from two fits of the same model (two seeds, or adjacent folds on shared bars) after aligning labels.
Rank correlation of a continuous score (anomaly score) between two fits of the same model on shared bars, with the overlap of the flagged sets.
Share of bars assigned to each state.
metrics.engineSource: state counts are logged to the terminal only

metrics.definition: Mean count of consecutive bars in the same state.

metrics.fullName: Outcome separation per group (state, score bin, flagged set or rule)
metrics.definition: For each group named by group_kind: the up share of scored bars minus the up share of all scored bars of the same series (or the same for the absolute forward move), with a moving-block bootstrap interval whose block is at least label_horizon_bars, and for rules the count of candidates tried.
metrics.engineSource: state, bin and rule membership per bar are not in the predictions table

metrics.fullName: Flagged share on unseen bars against the configured contamination
metrics.definition: Share of test bars beyond the training-fitted anomaly threshold against the model's contamination setting; a share far from the setting means the test bars drifted from the training bars.

metrics.fullName: Held-out reconstruction error as a share of feature variance
metrics.definition: Mean squared difference between unseen rows and their rebuilt version (the centroid or map node for codebook methods) over the features' total variance.
Share of each row's k nearest neighbours in the map that were neighbours in feature space (Venna-Kaski), k stated.
Share of each row's k nearest feature-space neighbours that stay neighbours in the map.
Exponential of the entropy of the normalised singular values of the embedding on unseen rows; a collapse detector.

metrics.fullName: Kullback-Leibler term of the evidence lower bound
metrics.definition: The divergence term reported apart from the reconstruction term.
Count of latent units whose posterior mean varies across rows; a posterior-collapse check.

metrics.fullName: Independence of components on held-out rows
metrics.definition: Mean absolute pairwise mutual information between the extracted components on unseen rows.
metrics.baseline: the same on the raw standardised features

metrics.definition: One minus the variance of the remainder over the variance of seasonal plus remainder.

metrics.fullName: Gain over the same model with its special part switched off
metrics.definition: The model's proper score minus the score of the same pipeline with one named part removed on the same folds; the record names the ablation.

metrics.fullName: Gain over the flat agent of the same learner
metrics.definition: Test-tape return of the hierarchical agent minus that of the same learning algorithm with no hierarchy, options or skills.

metrics.fullName: Option usage shares, duration and subgoal-reached share
metrics.definition: Share of bars under each option or skill; its companions option_duration_bars and subgoal_reached_fraction are separate registry ids.
Share of admitted pseudo-labels that match the masked true label, per round.

metrics.fullName: Admitted share of the unlabelled pool per round
metrics.definition: Unlabelled pool rows admitted over pool size, per round.

metrics.fullName: Classifier two-sample test accuracy (real versus generated)
metrics.definition: Held-out accuracy of a fresh judge, trained after the generator is frozen, at telling real validation-span rows from unseen generated rows; the judge is named (today a logistic regression on each feature and its square).
Share of generated rows inside the real rows' k-nearest-neighbour neighbourhood.
Share of real rows inside the generated rows' neighbourhood; near zero is mode collapse.
Median distance from generated rows to their nearest training row over the same median for held-out real rows; well below 1 means training rows are being copied.

metrics.fullName: Held-out denoising error by noise level
metrics.definition: Mean squared noise-prediction (or score) error on unseen rows at each noise level, weighting stated; it bounds the negative log-likelihood only under likelihood weighting.

Absolute differences between simulated and observed return kurtosis, autocorrelation of returns and of absolute returns, and the Wasserstein-1 distance between the return distributions; one row per statistic.
metrics.baseline: the same distances between two halves of the real series

metrics.definition: Standard deviation of the reported statistic across independent simulated paths over the square root of the path count, shown with the path count.

metrics.fullName: Markov chain Monte Carlo standard error
metrics.definition: Posterior standard deviation over the square root of the bulk effective sample size, because chain draws are autocorrelated.
Square root of pooled over within-chain variance for the worst parameter; the path simulator refuses a fit above its own gate, recorded with its source as a refusal rule, not a target.

metrics.fullName: Bulk and tail effective sample size
metrics.definition: Count of independent draws the chains are worth.

metrics.fullName: Validation-tape return used to pick the checkpoint
metrics.definition: Mean reward per decision of the kept policy on the validation span's tape; the kept policy is the maximum of this number over epochs, so it is optimistic.
metrics.engineSource: checkpoint selection in deep_value_agent, policy_agent, policy_search adapters

metrics.fullName: Mean test-tape return of the policy's own action
metrics.definition: Mean reward per decision of the frozen policy's own action, flat included, on the fold's test tape; reward is the whole horizon-bar trade opened at the next open, net of one round trip, over the decision bar's move scale; exact because the fixed tape pays every action.
metrics.baseline: always flat (0), always long, and uniform random action on the same tape

metrics.definition: Interquartile mean and interval of the headline number over runs of the same model on the same series that differ only in seed.

metrics.fullName: Predicted action value minus realised discounted return
metrics.definition: Mean over validation decisions of the value predicted for the action taken minus the realised return along the tape from that decision with the same discount_factor and step count as the training target; positive is optimistic. Not applicable to tabular planners.
One minus the variance of return minus value estimate over the variance of return.
Mean entropy of the policy's action probabilities; a collapse diagnostic.

metrics.fullName: Open-loop prediction error by step ahead
metrics.definition: Error of the world model's k-step-ahead prediction made without seeing the intervening bars, for each k, in the space the model predicts in (price or latent, named).
Mean reward of the policy inside the learned model minus on the real tape; positive is optimistic; defined only for action-conditioned models.

metrics.fullName: Expected minus realised utility of the recommended decision
metrics.definition: Expected utility the solver computed from its in-sample model minus the utility its decisions earned on later bars; positive is optimistic.
Return on a later time block after the allowed adaptation steps minus return on the same block from the shared start without adapting.
Best feasible objective minus best proven bound over the absolute best feasible objective; the duality gap for linear and quadratic programmes.
The approximation guarantee the selection method carries before seeing data (one minus one over e for lazy greedy on a monotone submodular objective); a bound, not a measurement.
Largest violation of a stated constraint by the returned point and by its dual, with the solver's termination status.

metrics.fullName: Best objective found by evaluation count
metrics.definition: Best training objective found so far against generations or evaluations.
metrics.baseline: random search with the same budget on the same objective
metrics.engineSource: policy_search writes negative utility of the best candidate into train_loss

metrics.fullName: Solver convergence residual and iteration count
metrics.definition: Largest change between sweeps or outer iterations (Bellman residual, belief-propagation residual), with search statistics.
Share of bars on which at least one non-default rule fires or a proof or feasible assignment exists, and per rule.
Share of test-bar predictions that violate none of the packages/config/cycle_rules.json rules the model was penalised on, and per rule.

metrics.fullName: Structure stability (edge, feature, formula or component recurrence)
metrics.definition: Share of refits (folds or bootstrap) in which each learned edge, selected feature, evolved formula or matched component reappears.
Rank correlation between the base ranking of alternatives and rankings after perturbing the criteria weights, with the smallest weight change that flips the top choice.

metrics.fullName: Maximum and upper-tail regret across scenarios
metrics.definition: Shortfall of the chosen strategy from the best strategy in each scenario, summarised by its maximum and a stated upper percentile.
Test bars the model made a call on in this scope.
Bars whose outcome is known and counted: the move over the label horizon beat the label threshold, the horizon crossed no session gap, and the model made a call.
metrics.formula: count of bars with a known up/down outcome and a prediction

metrics.definition: Processed bars left out of the classification metrics: the move stayed inside the label threshold, the horizon crossed a session gap, or the horizon ran past the data.
Bars whose label horizon crossed a session gap, so they carry no label, target or forecast.
metrics.formula: count of bars with crosses_gap true

metrics.definition: Of the bars called up, the share that went up.
metrics.formula: true up calls / all up calls

metrics.definition: Of the bars that went up, the share the model called up.
metrics.formula: true up calls / bars that went up

metrics.definition: Of the bars called down, the share that went down.
metrics.formula: true down calls / all down calls

metrics.definition: Of the bars that went down, the share the model called down (the specificity).
metrics.formula: true down calls / bars that went down

metrics.definition: The harmonic mean of precision and recall for the down class.
metrics.formula: 2 x true down / (2 x true down + false down calls + missed downs)

metrics.definition: The F1 score of up and of down, averaged.
Agreement between calls and outcomes beyond what the two base rates would give by chance.
Bars called up that went up.
Bars called up that went down.
Bars called down that went down.
Bars called down that went up.
The average probability of up the model gave on scored bars.
The Brier score of always forecasting the base rate; a property of the data, not the model. Brier = reliability - resolution + uncertainty, up to the spread of p inside each bin.
The accuracy of calling every scored bar up.
metrics.formula: scored bars that went up / scored bars

metrics.definition: Price forecasts whose target bar has been walked, so their error is known.
metrics.formula: count of bars with a forecast error

metrics.definition: The middle size of the forecast error; not moved by a few large misses.
What the calls earned before commissions, fees and slippage.
The average bar's net profit scaled to a year of bars.
metrics.formula: mean(per-bar net) x bars per year

metrics.definition: Net profit divided by the session days traded.
The mean net profit of one bar.
Bars marked to market in this scope.
CME session days with at least one bar in this scope.
Sharpe computed on each session day's net profit, annualized with 252 sessions per year.
metrics.formula: mean(day net) / std(day net, ddof 1) x sqrt(252)

metrics.definition: The size of the 95th-percentile bar gain over the 5th-percentile bar loss; above 1 the right tail is fatter.
metrics.formula: |95th percentile of r| / |5th percentile of r|

metrics.definition: Profit factor times tail ratio (Kestner): above 1 the edge survives its tails.
Net profit over the worst drawdown: how many times the profit covers its deepest hole.
The longest stretch the equity spent below a previous peak, from the peak until it was regained or the scope ended.
metrics.formula: max over drawdown episodes of bars from peak to recovery

metrics.definition: The longest time the equity spent below a previous peak, in calendar days; it can be a different episode from the longest in bars (a few bars across a weekend).
metrics.formula: max over drawdown episodes of (time of recovery, or of the last bar, - time of the peak) / 86,400 s

metrics.definition: Bars from the deepest trough back to the peak before it; null when the scope ended before the equity recovered.
metrics.formula: bars from trough to recovery of the deepest episode

metrics.definition: The average depth below the running peak over the bars spent under water.
metrics.formula: mean(running peak - equity) over bars below the peak

metrics.definition: The root mean square depth below the running peak over every bar: depth and duration of pain together (Martin and McCann 1989, in USD).
Distinct peak-to-trough-to-recovery episodes.
Closed trades with a positive net.
Closed trades with a negative net.
The average winner's size over the average loser's.
The mean net of a closed trade.
The mean net of a winning trade.
The mean net of a losing trade (negative).
The best closed trade.
The worst closed trade.
The winning trades' nets added up.
The losing trades' nets added up (negative).
The closed trades' nets added up.
How long a trade stayed open, on average.
How long winning trades stayed open.
How long losing trades stayed open.
The most winning trades in a row.
metrics.formula: longest run of consecutive winners, in entry order

metrics.definition: The most losing trades in a row.
metrics.formula: longest run of consecutive losers, in entry order

metrics.definition: Van Tharp's measure of how steady the trade results are: the average trade over its spread, times the square root of the trade count (uncapped).
metrics.formula: sqrt(trades) x mean(trade net) / std(trade net, ddof 1)

metrics.definition: The share of bars held long.
The share of bars held short.
The share of bars with no position.
The round-trip cost of a trade, on average.
What one contract costs to enter or exit once.
metrics.formula: median over trades of cost / (2 x contracts)

metrics.fullName: Costs' share of the pre-cost profit
metrics.definition: How much of what the calls earned went to costs; above 1 the costs took more than the edge.
metrics.formula: total cost / net profit before costs

metrics.fullName: Gain over the same agent without the graph encoder
metrics.definition: Mean test-tape return per decision of the frozen graph-encoder agent minus that of the same learning algorithm, state design and folds with the graph layers removed so it reads the unmixed node features; the registry's gain_over_flat_agent_of_same_learner covers only the removal of a hierarchy, and gain_over_own_ablation is a difference of proper scores that a reward-trained agent does not have.
metrics.formula: R_graph_encoder - R_without_graph_encoder, each the mean reward per decision of the frozen policy's own action on the fold's test tape

metrics.definition: Mean over the hidden token positions of rows the model never trained on of minus the natural logarithm of the probability the model gave to the true token, given the visible tokens of the same row; the masking rule and the mask probability are stated with it.
metrics.formula: minus the mean over hidden positions of ln q(true token given the visible tokens)

metrics.fullName: Adjusted Rand index of the groups against held-back labels
metrics.definition: On rows whose labels were hidden from the fit, the chance-corrected share of row pairs that the fitted grouping and the held-back label classes treat the same way (both together or both apart); zero is the agreement of two unrelated partitions and one is identical partitions. Cluster purity and normalised mutual information against the same labels are companion readings. The specification of semi-supervised clustering names these as its evaluation; the registry's assignment_stability_adjusted_rand_index compares two fits of the same model with each other and cannot stand in for it.
metrics.formula: pair agreements minus the pair agreements expected by chance, divided by the largest possible pair agreements minus the pair agreements expected by chance, over pairs of held-back rows
metrics.units: index, zero for chance-level agreement and one for identical partitions

metrics.definition: Pearson correlation, over every pair of rows, between the original distance of the two rows and the cophenetic distance, which is the merge height at which the agglomerative tree first places the two rows in one branch; it measures how faithfully the dendrogram preserves the pairwise distances it was built from, and the divisive direction by bisecting k-means has no merge heights to read it from.
metrics.formula: correlation over row pairs (i, j) of d(i, j) and the merge height at which i and j first share a branch

metrics.definition: One minus the squared Pearson correlation between the pairwise shortest-path distances along the neighbour graph and the pairwise straight-line distances between the mapped points, over the rows the map was fitted on; zero means the map reproduces the graph distances exactly. The fit measure Isomap is judged by, for the Isomap setting only.
metrics.formula: 1 - corr(D_G, D_Y)^2, with D_G the graph shortest-path distances and D_Y the map distances over all pairs of fitted rows
metrics.baseline: the same graph distances set against the straight-line distances among the original feature rows

metrics.definition: Sum over the fitted rows of the squared distance between each mapped point and the weighted blend of its neighbours' mapped points, using the weights learned among the feature rows; the quantity the second step of locally linear embedding minimises, equal to the sum of the retained eigenvalues. The coordinates are constrained to unit covariance, and the cost is comparable only between fits with the same neighbour count and coordinate count. For the locally linear embedding setting only.
metrics.formula: sum over i of the squared norm of (y_i - sum over j of W_ij y_j), with W learned among the feature rows

metrics.fullName: Dice overlap of the marked zone
metrics.definition: Twice the number of held-out positions that both the map marks as inside a zone and the labels place inside it, divided by the number the map marks plus the number the labels place inside; it is the F-one score of the inside-the-zone call on a binary mask, and the intersection over union follows from it as the Dice overlap divided by two minus the Dice overlap. It is read beside the share of positions labelled inside a zone.

metrics.fullName: Share of restarts that end in the best basin found
metrics.definition: Share of the search's restarts whose final training objective lies within the adapter's stated tolerance of the lowest objective any restart reached; a heuristic confidence signal named by the non-convex optimisation specification, never a proof of global optimality. The basin-hopping searcher already computes it as best_basin_share in its search statistics.
metrics.formula: count of restarts with final objective within the tolerance of the minimum over restarts, divided by the count of restarts with a finite final objective

metrics.definition: Mean over unseen rows and over nodes of the natural logarithm of the probability the fitted undirected graphical model gives to each node's observed state given the observed states of its neighbours; the conditional quantity the pseudo-likelihood fit raises, reported where the joint likelihood needs an intractable partition function.
metrics.formula: mean over rows t and nodes i of log p(x_ti given the neighbours of node i), taken on rows the potentials were not fitted on

metrics.fullName: Mean option, goal or directive run length in bars
metrics.definition: For each option, goal or directive: the mean count of consecutive test bars it stays in force from the bar it is started to the bar it terminates or is replaced.
metrics.formula: Test bars spent under the option divided by the number of times the option was started on test bars.

metrics.fullName: Share of started goals the lower level reached
metrics.definition: Of the goals or subgoals the upper level started on test bars, the share for which the model's own goal-achievement test returned true before the goal's step budget expired, overall and per goal.
metrics.formula: Goals reached before their step budget expired divided by goals started, on test bars.

metrics.fullName: Mean cosine between the realised latent change and the goal direction
metrics.definition: For a feudal agent whose goal is a direction in latent space: the mean over test bars of the cosine between the encoder's latent change across the goal horizon and the goal that was in force, which is the lower level's own training reward measured on bars it did not train on.
metrics.formula: Mean over test bars of the cosine of the angle between the latent state at the end of the goal horizon minus the latent state at its start, and the goal vector issued at its start.
metrics.units: cosine between minus one and one

metrics.fullName: Share of held-out bars where the selector's top choice matches the demonstrated sub-policy
metrics.definition: For a hierarchy whose upper level is first fitted by imitation: the share of held-out demonstration bars, separated from the training span by the purge and embargo, on which the selector's highest-probability sub-policy equals the sub-policy the demonstration recorded, measured at the end of the imitation stage and again after fine-tuning.
metrics.formula: Held-out demonstration bars where the selector's top-ranked sub-policy equals the demonstrated sub-policy divided by held-out demonstration bars.

metrics.fullName: Share of sampled skill points the discriminator identifies from the bars visited
metrics.definition: On unseen bars, for each skill point on a grid of sampled skill points, the skill-conditioned policy plays that point as a trajectory and the discriminator names the skill point it infers from the visited bars; the value is the share of grid points whose inferred skill point is closest to the one that was played, compared with the chance level of one divided by the number of grid points.
metrics.formula: count(grid points whose inferred skill point is nearest the played skill point) / count(grid points), on unseen bars

metrics.fullName: Gap between a skill's observed success share and its start-region classifier's stated chance
metrics.definition: On unseen rollouts, started at states the start-region classifier admits, the rollouts are grouped by the classifier's stated chance that the skill reaches the next start region; the value is the rollout-weighted mean absolute difference between each group's observed share of rollouts that reached it and the group's mean stated chance.
metrics.formula: sum over groups of (rollouts in group / all rollouts) * abs(observed success share - mean stated success chance), on unseen rollouts

metrics.fullName: Share of reward variance the basis outcomes leave unexplained
metrics.definition: On rows held out from the weight fit, the variance of the realised reward minus the basis outcomes times the fitted reward weights, divided by the variance of the realised reward; it shows how far the reward departs from the weighted sum of basis outcomes that successor features assume.
metrics.formula: variance(reward - basis_outcomes . reward_weights) / variance(reward), on held-out rows

metrics.fullName: Distance between the policy weights generated for different contexts
metrics.definition: For a hypernetwork that writes a policy's weights from a context, the mean Euclidean distance between the full generated weight vectors of pairs of unseen contexts, divided by the mean norm of a generated weight vector; zero means the hypernetwork writes one fixed policy whatever the context.
metrics.formula: mean over context pairs (i, j) of norm(theta_i - theta_j) divided by mean over contexts of norm(theta_i), where theta is the flattened generated weight vector

metrics.fullName: Kullback-Leibler divergence of each task policy from the shared distilled policy
metrics.definition: For a multitask agent with one policy per task and one shared distilled policy, the mean over a task's unseen bars of the Kullback-Leibler divergence of the task policy's action distribution from the shared policy's, reported per task; zero means the task policy is the shared policy.
metrics.formula: per task i: mean over bars of sum over actions a of pi_i(a given s) times (ln pi_i(a given s) minus ln pi_0(a given s))

metrics.fullName: Mean learned noise scale of the noisy layers
metrics.definition: Mean absolute value of the learned noise-scale parameters over every weight and bias of the noisy linear layers of the value head at the kept epoch, shown beside the value it started from under the initial_noise_scale setting; a scale trained down to nothing means the network stopped exploring by its own choice. The deep value agent already computes it for the fit log (deep_value_agent/adapter.py, mean_noise_scale in fit_summary) and records it in no metric table.
metrics.formula: mean over noisy weights and biases of abs(noise_scale)

metrics.definition: Mean over validation decisions of the absolute difference between the two critics' values for the actor's own noise-free position; where it is large the minimum of the two critics is doing real work and the value behind the position is unreliable. Defined only for agents with two critics.
metrics.formula: mean over decisions of abs(Q_1(s, mu(s)) - Q_2(s, mu(s)))

metrics.definition: Mean and spread over test bars of the curvature term of the normalised advantage function, which is how fast the predicted value falls as the position moves away from the network's preferred position; near zero the network sees no difference between long and short, very large it is certain or ill-conditioned. With one action dimension the curvature matrix is a single positive number per bar.
metrics.formula: mean over bars of P(s), where Q(s, a) = V(s) - P(s) (a - mu(s))^2 / 2
metrics.units: move-scale reward units per squared position unit

metrics.fullName: Mean spread of the search distribution by generation
metrics.definition: For a search that refits a diagonal Gaussian to its elite candidates each generation, the mean over the searched weights of the standard deviation of that Gaussian after each generation, traced against the generation number; a spread that shrinks and flattens means the search settled, and a spread held up by the variance floor means it stopped shrinking only because of the floor.
metrics.formula: per generation: mean over searched weights of the standard deviation of the refitted Gaussian
metrics.units: the units of the searched weight

metrics.definition: For a clipped-surrogate policy update, the share of sampled actions in the update whose ratio of new to old action probability fell outside the clip band, reported per update and averaged over the passes of that rollout; near zero means the clip never bound, and a persistently high share means the clip is limiting most of the step.
metrics.formula: per update: mean over sampled actions of the indicator that the probability ratio lies outside one minus the clip range to one plus the clip range

metrics.fullName: Realised mean Kullback-Leibler divergence per policy update
metrics.definition: For a policy update under a divergence limit, the mean over the rollout's states of the Kullback-Leibler divergence of the new policy's action distribution from the old policy's, measured after the accepted step and reported against the limit the line search was allowed to reach.
metrics.formula: per update: mean over rollout states of the sum over actions a of old policy probability of a times the difference of the natural logarithms of the old and the new probability of a

metrics.fullName: Consistency ratio of the pairwise comparison matrix
metrics.definition: For criterion weights derived by the analytic hierarchy process: the consistency index of the pairwise comparison matrix divided by the random index for a matrix of the same size; zero means the pairwise judgments never contradict one another. It is zero by construction when the matrix is built from ratios of a single importance vector, as the runnable multi_criteria_decision_analysis adapter does.
metrics.formula: (principal eigenvalue minus criterion count) divided by (criterion count minus one), then divided by the random index for that criterion count

metrics.fullName: Share of scenarios in which the strategy performs acceptably
metrics.definition: For one candidate strategy: the number of scenarios in the ensemble whose simulated performance reaches the stated acceptable threshold divided by the number of scenarios; robust decision making ranks strategies by it. Shown with the threshold and the scenario count; the scenarios of the runnable adapter are overlapping re-cuts of the training span.
metrics.formula: count of scenarios with utility at or above the acceptable threshold divided by the count of scenarios

metrics.definition: Of all scenarios in which the strategy fails its acceptable threshold, the share that fall inside the region of uncertain inputs the scenario-discovery step returned (Bryant and Lempert 2010).
metrics.formula: failing scenarios inside the discovered region divided by all failing scenarios

metrics.definition: Of all scenarios inside the region of uncertain inputs the scenario-discovery step returned, the share in which the strategy fails its acceptable threshold (Bryant and Lempert 2010); read with coverage and the number of conditions that define the region.
metrics.formula: failing scenarios inside the discovered region divided by all scenarios inside the region

metrics.definition: Mean, over orders present in both the replay and the live or paper-trading log, of the realised fill price minus the simulated fill price, signed by the order's side so that a positive value means the replay filled the order at a better price than the market gave, in ticks, shown with the order count.
metrics.formula: mean(side * (realised_fill_price - simulated_fill_price)) / tick_size, side = +1 for a buy and -1 for a sell

metrics.definition: Share of the walks (or cases) a survival model was fitted or scored on whose event was not observed before the watch ended, because the maximum hold, a session gap or the end of the data came first.
metrics.formula: censored walks divided by all walks

metrics.fullName: Proportional hazards test on scaled Schoenfeld residuals (p-value)
metrics.definition: Grambsch-Therneau test that the scaled Schoenfeld residuals of each fitted covariate, and of all covariates jointly, are unrelated to elapsed time, with the time transform stated; a small value says the covariate's effect on the hazard changes over the walk.
metrics.formula: chi-square test of zero slope in the regression of scaled Schoenfeld residuals on the stated transform of event time

metrics.fullName: Share of bars on which the model's own trade gate is open
metrics.definition: Bars on which the model's own trade gate is open, divided by the bars the model made a call on. The gate is open on a bar only when the fold is certified (the one-sided 95 percent lower bound of the realisation slope, measured on purged out-of-fold training rows, is above zero) and the call's expected gain in points exceeds one round trip of costs, so the share is zero for a whole fold that is not certified; the adapter also computes it on the validation rows and each recorded regime forecast row carries the gate state.
metrics.formula: count of bars with an open gate (fold certified, and realisation slope times claimed gain above the round trip cost in points), divided by count of bars with a call

objectives.plainWords: Punishes the model by how little probability it gave to what happened; unweighted, so the output tracks the base rate.

objectives.formula: BCEWithLogits with pos_weight = negatives/positives, or class_weight balanced
objectives.plainWords: Same, with each class carrying half the loss, so 0.5 means above the 50/50 prior (networks.py:915-919; models.py:711,982).

objectives.fullName: Regularised boosting objective on logarithmic loss
objectives.formula: sum log loss + per tree (gamma*leaves + 0.5*lambda*sum w^2)
objectives.plainWords: Trees added one at a time, each correcting the last, with a penalty on tree size.
Logistic regression with a normal curve.
Probability spread over several classes, ordered or not.
A regression whose noise grows with its level.
Find the widest street between up bars and down bars.

objectives.formula: T_k max(0, m_plus - |v_k|)^2 + lambda(1-T_k) max(0, |v_k| - m_minus)^2
objectives.plainWords: Make the right class's capsule long and the wrong one short.

objectives.formula: choose the split minimising weighted child impurity
objectives.plainWords: Keep cutting the bars into purer groups.
Nothing is minimised: neighbours vote, counts are tallied, rules are authored, or an estimator is closed form.
Model what up bars and down bars each look like, then ask which this bar resembles.
Draw the line with the smallest squared misses; targets the mean.
Squared for small misses, absolute for big ones.
Aims at a chosen percentile.

objectives.formula: components maximising cov(Xw, y), then regression
objectives.plainWords: Compress features toward what moves with the target.
Fit the rhythm of the return series and its volatility.

objectives.fullName: Additive series decomposition by local smoothing
objectives.plainWords: Split the series into a slow part, a repeating part and what is left.

objectives.formula: log int p(y|w)p(w)dw; or draws from p(w|y)
objectives.plainWords: Weigh every plausible setting by how well it explains the data.
Rebuild the input through a noisy code kept close to a prior; variational models only.

objectives.fullName: Exact negative log-likelihood of a density
objectives.plainWords: Put probability exactly where real rows fall.
Learn to remove noise added on purpose.
Make real rows low-energy and the model's own samples high-energy.

objectives.formula: min_G max_D E log D(real) + E log(1 - D(G(z)))
objectives.plainWords: A forger and a detective train against each other; no density, no bound.
Squeeze the row through a narrow neck and rebuild it.

objectives.formula: KL or cross-entropy between neighbour graphs; geodesic stress
objectives.plainWords: Keep near rows near after flattening.
Unmix the features into sources that move independently.
Explain each row as an additive blend of parts.
Solve an invented puzzle with no labels.
Pull windows with the same outcome together and push the others apart; reads labels.

objectives.fullName: Supervised loss plus an unlabelled-data term
objectives.plainWords: Learn from the labelled bars and behave sensibly on the masked ones.
Group rows so members are close and groups are apart.

objectives.formula: sum log sum_k w_k N_k(x); forward-algorithm log p(x_1..T)
objectives.plainWords: Explain the bars as a blend of a few moods.
Score how unlike the training bars a bar is.

objectives.formula: partial likelihood; log f(t) observed + log S(t) censored
objectives.plainWords: Model how long until a barrier is touched, counting open walks correctly.

objectives.fullName: Task loss plus rule or auxiliary penalty
objectives.plainWords: Predict well while being charged for contradicting the rule library.
Learn what each action is worth by correcting the last guess with the reward.
Make rewarded actions more likely; the clipped surrogate is PPO's alone.

objectives.fullName: World-model loss plus imagined or planned return
objectives.formula: reconstruction + reward likelihood - KL, then return in the model
objectives.plainWords: Learn a replay of the market, then practise in it.
Learn a start that tunes quickly to the next block.

objectives.fullName: Return of a policy over options with learned termination or subgoals
objectives.formula: E[sum r] over manager and worker policies
objectives.plainWords: A manager picks a sub-policy or goal; a worker carries it out.

objectives.fullName: Net utility of positions on the training reward tape
objectives.plainWords: Search a position rule for the most money on the training tape after costs.

objectives.fullName: The stated mathematical programme over signal weights
objectives.formula: max c'x s.t. Ax<=b and variants
objectives.plainWords: Solve a stated weighting problem exactly.
Keep adding the signal that helps most; fast, with at most an a-priori guarantee.

objectives.fullName: Maximum expected utility or Bellman optimality on a fitted model
objectives.plainWords: Given an estimated model of the world, compute its best decision.
Tune a simulator until its fake tape has the real tape's fingerprints.

objectives.fullName: Ranking by stated weights or minimax regret
objectives.plainWords: Order options by weights a person chose.

objectives.fullName: Cross-entropy on outcome energies plus a weighted energy contrast with sampled negatives
objectives.formula: cross_entropy(f(x), y) + generative_weight * ( -mean(logsumexp_k f(x_real)[k]) + mean(logsumexp_k f(x_negative)[k]) + energy_penalty * ( mean(logsumexp_k f(x_real)[k]^2) + mean(logsumexp_k f(x_negative)[k]^2) ) ), where x_negative comes from short-run stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics started from a persistent replay buffer and x_real is the labelled batch plus unlabelled training-span rows (adapters_extra/density_classifier/energy.py:76-102)
objectives.plainWords: Call the direction right on labelled bars, and at the same time make real rows low-energy and the model's own Langevin samples high-energy; unweighted, so the output tracks the base rate.

objectives.fullName: Cross-entropy plus an entropy penalty on the leaf mass distribution
objectives.formula: mean over rows of the cross-entropy of the forward label against the probability formed from the mass-weighted mixture of leaf logits (squared error for the return variant), plus leaf_entropy_weight times (the natural logarithm of the leaf count minus the entropy in nats of the leaf mass distribution)
objectives.plainWords: Predict the forward label well, and be charged whenever the routing sends nearly all mass to one leaf, so the decision graph keeps more than one route in use; unweighted, so the output tracks the base rate.

objectives.fullName: Class-weighted cross-entropy plus an entropy penalty on the batch mean leaf mass
objectives.formula: BCEWithLogits on the mixed leaf logit with pos_weight = negatives/positives, plus leaf_entropy_weight times (the natural logarithm of decision_width minus the entropy in nats of the batch mean leaf mass), the penalty added to every training batch's loss (networks.py:987-990; networks_extra/feature_graph.py:447-458)
objectives.plainWords: Same as class-weighted binary cross-entropy, so 0.5 means above the even prior, with an added charge for letting the routing collapse onto few leaves; the penalty is on the training curve only.

objectives.fullName: Total cost of one path built through a construction graph
objectives.formula: minimise the summed edge cost along one complete path built step by step, where each step is drawn with probability proportional to pheromone strength to a power times heuristic desirability to a power and each deposit is proportional to the inverse of the finished path cost
objectives.plainWords: Find the cheapest complete path or ordering by letting many ants build paths and reinforce the edges of the cheap ones.

objectives.fullName: Pseudo-likelihood of an undirected graphical model
objectives.formula: sum over rows t and nodes i of log p(x_ti given the neighbours of node i), optionally minus lambda times the squared potentials
objectives.plainWords: Teach every node to predict itself from its neighbours, which avoids adding up every joint configuration of the whole graph.

objectives.fullName: Hinge-loss Markov random field energy with learned rule weights
objectives.formula: E(y) = sum over rules r of w_r * max(0, body_r - head_r)^p with p in {1, 2}; inference returns argmin over y in [0, 1] of E(y); weight learning moves each w_r by the learning rate times (distance of rule r at the inferred state minus its distance at the observed outcome), less weight decay, floored at zero
objectives.plainWords: Each soft rule is charged for how far the current truth values are from satisfying it; inference finds the truth values with the smallest total charge, and learning raises the weight of rules the observed outcome satisfies better than the model's own answer.

objectives.fullName: Least absolute error, optionally with a parsimony penalty
objectives.formula: mean over rows of the absolute value of (y - f(x)), plus penalty times node count during selection
objectives.plainWords: Find the formula with the smallest average miss, counting every point of error the same; targets the median.

asRunRules: R0 Source of truth. One id per quantity: the registry id. It equals the engine id wherever the engine id is already full words (sharpe_ratio, accuracy, price_forecast_skill, majority_class_accuracy); only log_loss, roc_auc, f1_score, f1_score_down and macro_f1_score get full-word registry ids, mapped in packages/config/metric_registry.json by an engine_ids array. The registry holds all 102 report.py DEFINITIONS keys one-to-one (a parity test fails otherwise); this taxonomy lists the ones a profile or rule names. As-run text never restates a formula. How P(up) is formed comes from adapter code, not direction.probability (catalog.py:63).

R1 Every runnable model (272, including regime_montecarlo_decision) is measured on the same scoreboard. 'Meaningful' means the number tests something this model's mechanism produced; everything else is listed under measured_not_meaningful with a reason.

R2 Trading metrics. The position follows the sign of the latest call (long when P(up) is at least 0.5); a trade ends when the call flips, a stop or target is hit, or the fold ends; a same-direction call at holding expiry is kept with no cost; a bar with no prediction holds the position (simulate.py:262-392; engine.py:1440-1443). Each as_run block records the dials in force: long_only, holding_bars, stop_loss_ticks, take_profit_ticks, contracts. Meaningful for all models as 'this model's direction call under the engine's rule'. predicted_up_fraction and trade_count are shown beside every trading metric. For agents add: the agent's own flat action, sizing and holding period are overridden.

R2b Trading references. buy_and_hold_net_profit_usd and the sign-shuffled baseline are the only same-series references; 0 for Sharpe, Sortino and Calmar and 1 for profit factor are arithmetic markers, not no-skill references, because a random-direction trader pays costs. exposure_fraction and the long, short and flat shares are measured_not_meaningful when long_only is false and no stop or target is set.

R3 Hard-call metrics (type threshold_classification) are meaningful for all models with the caveat that they depend on the scale and prior of P(up); for class-weighted and validation-curve models that is the fitted prior, not the model's own.

R4 Probability-magnitude metrics by probability_source, one value per MODEL KEY in the metric registry (generated from adapter code, diffed against direction.probability in a test), plus the boolean class_weighted. own_likelihood_probability (xgboost, lightgbm, catboost, gradient boosting, SGD, probit, sklearn MLP, binomial GLM, ordinal, multinomial, tweedie, gradient_descent, interior_point_method, naive_bayes with the note that independence makes it over-confident, adversarial_autoencoder class head, semi-supervised networks): logarithmic_loss primary. class_weighted true (shared neural loop and its copies, logistic_regression, self-supervised probe): class_balanced_logarithmic_loss primary, ln 2 the reference, calibration against the base rate measured_not_meaningful. frequency_or_vote_share (k-NN, single trees, random_forest and extra_trees with class_weighted true, latent_state_readout Beta-smoothed up-rates, graph label shares, markov_chain path share, kaplan_meier_barrier, siamese neighbour share, cross_entropy_method_policy rule share): brier_score is the proper score, logarithmic_loss is measured_not_meaningful, extreme_probability_bar_count recorded. validation_fitted_curve (from_price models, SVM, decision_graph, path_simulator, policy_search except gradient_descent, signal_program except interior_point_method, symbolic_reasoner, calibrated_classifier, manifold_regularization, TSVM, cycle GAN, gamma, poisson, zero-inflated Poisson, successor features, all density_classifier variants as Bayes posterior plus one fitted temperature): meaningful for model-plus-curve; the fitted parameters saw validation rows. validation_temperature_only (deep_value_agent, discrete_state_agent planners and tabular, state_space_abstraction, action_conditioned_dynamics_transformer, DDPG, TD3, NAF): measured_not_meaningful as a forecast probability. model_implied_tail_probability (bayesian_predictive, series_forecast, multivariate_regression, cox_proportional_hazards, accelerated_failure_time, mixture_of_exponentials): meaningful, the cleanest test of the model's own distribution. policy_action_share (policy_agent discrete, SAC, meta_agent, world_model_agent shares): measured_not_meaningful. classifier_trained_on_generated_rows (six synthetic-route GANs), learned_head_on_code (latent_projection_head), mean_of_base_learners (pseudo_label_ensemble, stacked_generalization, attention_weighted_forecast_stack): meaningful for the named readout. regime_montecarlo_decision: assigned from its adapter when its owning session lands it.

R5 Ranking metrics are meaningful where the score is continuous. distinct_probability_level_count is computed per fold at run time; the static record says only 'level count may be small' for kaplan_meier_barrier, single trees, first-match decision lists, binned graphs and linear_programming.
